title: Accelerating Intra-Node GPU Communication: A Performance Model for Multi-Path Transfers
problem: GPU-to-GPU intra-node communication bottleneck in MPI applications; unclear how to optimally distribute P2P transfers across multiple communication paths.
motivation: Multi-path GPU communication (via NVLink, PCIe, etc.) can improve throughput if routed optimally; MPI+UCX currently lacks guidance for path selection.
method: When GPUs in the same computer send data to each other, they can use multiple communication paths simultaneously. This model predicts how fast data will actually move by accounting for the speed of each communication link (link bandwidth), the delay cost of managing multiple data flows (pipeline overhead), and the need to coordinate different data streams so they don't interfere with each other (stream synchronization). By understanding these factors, it determines the best way to split up the data transfer across available paths to minimize total transfer time.
key_novelty: The key insight is a mathematical model that accurately predicts the fastest way to split GPU data transfers across multiple paths—within 6% accuracy.
contributions: Performance model for multi-path GPU-to-GPU communication
Increased throughput via intelligent path distribution
primary_theme: Performance model for optimal multi-path intra-node GPU communication
